To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in infected cells LSD1 is partially degraded or stably associated with the repressor complex; the repressor complex is recruited to the ND10 nuclear domain; and ICP8 accumulates at the ND10 periphery.
ICP0 depletes the lysine-specific histone demethylase LSD1, HDAC1, and CoREST from ND10 bodies, enabling viral DNA to be released from the repressor complex.
the repressor complex accumulates in the cytoplasm in infected cells and that ICP0 and the repressor complex interact in structures that abutt ND10 bodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the early events in HSV-1 replication and the role of the repressor and ICP0 in this process.
the dynamic interactions between ICP0, the ND10 bodies, the repressor complex components, viral DNA, and ICP8.
the dynamic interactions between viral and cellular proteins that are essential for the initiation of viral DNA replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ICP0-mediated disruption of the LSD1/CoREST complex is an important early event that facilitates the formation of the viral DNA replication compartments.
the repressor component and viral DNA-protein structures are juxtaposed, with ICP0 acting as a bridge to accomplish the necessary functions.
the repressor complex is recruited to viral DNA, where it is dislodged by ICP0 and then is translocated to the replication compartments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ICP0 is required for the reorganization of ND10 and for the recruitment of ICP0 and the viral replication complex into replication compartments.
ICP0 is essential for the formation of replication compartments and that the repressor complex is a critical component of that process.
HSV-1 has evolved mechanisms that allow it to overcome the silencing of viral genes and to initiate DNA replication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the repressor complex plays an important role in the establishment of the viral DNA replication compartment.
the repressor complex is an important component in the remodeling of the DNA-protein complex and in the initiation of viral DNA replication.
the viral DNA-proteins complexes are dynamic structures that interact with other nuclear bodies in order to accomplish the early steps in viral replication.
